transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. I came in because I’ve been having trouble keeping my focus at work. I’ll be scheduling appointments or working on the lobby displays, and I suddenly lose my place. It’s like my mind slips off because I’m thinking about what I might have missed or overlooked.
Do you get repeated unwanted thoughts that you may have missed or done something wrong, even when you try not to think about it?
Yes. I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but the thought just keeps looping anyway. Then it turns into one concern after another, and I end up checking details in my head over and over.
Do these thoughts feel intrusive and unwanted, like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Yes, that’s what it feels like. I can try to tell myself it’s already handled, but the thought still keeps coming back. Then it sort of jumps to the next thing I might have missed, and I end up going over details in my head again and again.
When those thoughts show up, do you feel driven to check things again?

Yes, I do. I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but it doesn’t really stop. The thought keeps looping, and then I move on to another concern, and pretty soon I’m checking the details in my head over and over.
Do you find yourself physically checking things again and again, like re-reading schedules or rechecking your work?

Yes, I do. I’m still showing up and getting through the day, but scheduling takes me longer now because I keep double-checking myself. And with the lobby displays, I’ve had to redo parts because I lose track of what I was arranging.
Do these thoughts feel like they don’t really make sense, but you still can’t stop them?

Yes. I know some of it doesn’t really make sense because I’ve already handled it, but it still keeps going. I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s done,” and then the thought loops anyway, and before long I’m on to the next concern and checking details in my head again.
About how much time each day do these repeated thoughts and checking take up?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t timed it. It’s kind of spread out through the day, a few minutes here and there when something comes up. It doesn’t feel like it takes over the whole day, but it does slow me down.
When you don’t double-check, does it feel like something bad might happen?

Yes, that’s kind of what it feels like. Like if I don’t check, some small thing might slip through—a schedule mix-up, a bill, travel details, or even a paperwork error—and then it could turn into a bigger problem than it should be.
When you do check again, does it briefly relieve the anxiety?

Yeah, briefly it does. I’ll check something and feel a little better for a minute, like, “Okay, it’s handled.” But then the thought can keep looping anyway, and pretty soon I’m thinking about the next thing and checking details in my head again.
Did these symptoms start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?
Yes. It’s been about nine months now, and it started after that overnight detention and the paperwork mix-up around it. That’s when I noticed all this really beginning.
Are these worries mostly about that detention and paperwork incident, or do they also happen about lots of other everyday things?

It started with that detention and paperwork thing, but now it’s definitely spread to other stuff. I worry about ordinary things like work schedules, bills, travel plans, little paperwork errors… like one small mix-up could turn into a much bigger problem.
Would you say these worries feel hard to control?

Yes, they do. I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” and I’ll mean it, but the thought still keeps looping. Then I’ve moved from one concern to another, and I’m checking details in my head over and over again.
Do you feel compelled to double-check things to make the anxiety from those thoughts go away?

Yes, kind of. It’s not always like I physically go check something, but in my head I keep going back over the details to try to calm myself down. I’ll tell myself it’s handled, but the thought keeps looping, and then I’m on to the next worry.
Do you feel like you have to check things in a certain specific way or until it feels just right?
I don’t think so, not in a specific way. It’s more like I keep mentally reviewing things because I feel uneasy, but I don’t have a set routine or a “just right” point that I’m trying to reach.
Do you often feel physically tense or keyed up?

Yes. Even when I’m at the front desk and I’m smiling and helping people, inside I feel really wound tight. My shoulders get tense, like they’re up around my ears, and I’m kind of braced, like I’m waiting for something to go wrong.
Do these worries usually feel excessive to you, like more than the situation really calls for?

Yes, I think they do. I’ll worry about pretty ordinary things—like my work schedule, bills, travel plans, or even a small paperwork mistake—and in my mind it turns into this bigger problem, like one little mix-up could cause a lot of trouble. It feels like more than the situation really calls for.
Are the thoughts mostly about making a mistake or missing something?

Mostly, yes—making a mistake or overlooking something is a big part of it. But it’s also broader than that. I worry about regular things like my work schedule, bills, travel plans, or small paperwork errors, like one little mix-up could turn into a much bigger problem.
Have these hard-to-control worries about different everyday things been present more days than not for at least six months?
Yes. It’s been more days than not, for about nine months now. It really started after that overnight detention and the paperwork mix-up around it, and it just kind of kept going.
Do these thoughts ever feel senseless or unreasonable to you, even while you still can’t stop them?

Yes, sometimes I know it doesn’t really make sense. I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but the thought just keeps looping anyway. Then I go from one concern to another, and before I know it I’m checking details in my head over and over.
Do these thoughts feel like they come into your mind against your will?

Yes, kind of. I don’t feel like I’m choosing to think about it. I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but it keeps looping anyway. Then it jumps from one concern to another, and I end up going over details in my head again and again.
